requirements.title: The /graph page shall display a static "why build this" explainer section describing second-brain/dynamic-context benefits and how graph visualization surfaces missing links

vision.paraphrase: Explainer section explains the second-brain concept and demonstrates how graph visualization surfaces content gaps.

conops.paraphrase: A visitor reads the 'why build this' explainer section describing second-brain benefits.
A visitor reads the explainer section describing second-brain benefits and how graph visualization surfaces missing links.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall allow a visitor to filter the visible nodes by status value (active, revisiting, dormant)

vision.paraphrase: Status dot must be sortable and filterable by visitors to explore nodes by engagement level.

conops.paraphrase: A visitor filters nodes by status (e.g., 'dormant') to identify under-connected content.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall allow a visitor to filter or sort the visible nodes by folder/taxonomy cluster

vision.paraphrase: Node grouping must be filterable so visitors can explore content clusters.

conops.paraphrase: A visitor filters nodes by folder/taxonomy cluster to explore related content groups.

requirements.title: The /graph page shall visually indicate a node's edge count so a visitor can identify under-connected nodes relative to their cluster peers

conops.paraphrase: A visitor notices a node with markedly fewer edges than cluster peers, identifying it as under-connected.

requirements.title: The side panel shall display a node's full related-node list so a visitor can recognize when a concept that logically should connect to other nodes currently does not

conops.paraphrase: A visitor recognizes a concept that logically should connect to other nodes but doesn't yet, by directly observing the sparse related-node list the side panel displays for that node.

requirements.title: The /graph page's explainer section shall name the layout mode in which each affordance it describes actually exists, and shall not describe an affordance as available in a mode that does not offer it

vision.paraphrase: Explainer accuracy fixes issue #4 finding A8, ensuring the copy matches the UI that actually exists; describing a control the reader cannot find costs trust.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor reads the explainer, it explicitly names the layout mode offering each affordance (e.g., 'filtering is available in force-directed mode'), preventing false promises about features that only exist elsewhere.
